title: Dispatch tokens: format, draft and verify, signed by the operator's root (decision 1, option 5)
description: First build task of the identity design the operator ratified on 2026-10-21. Tokens only; no wiring.
acceptance_criteria: A new tool, .harness/bin/token.py (another name only if it collides; justify), with at least: draft, which any agent may run and which emits an UNSIGNED token set for one epic, one token per (agent_name, task_id, role, issued_at, expiry, nonce), and prints the exact ssh-keygen -Y sign command the operator runs, mirroring warrant.py draft; and verify, which checks a presented token against the enrolled root (.harness/trust/root.pub), its expiry, and that the presented (agent, task, role) match.

The signature is an SSH signature by the operator's root key with a namespace distinct from warrants'. Never an HMAC or any shared secret: under D-17 every agent could read it. A test asserts that no code path in the module can sign, the same shape as warrant.py's.
Grain: one signed file per epic carrying that epic's tokens (ruling 2026-10-21). A token is valid only if its epic file's signature verifies against the enrolled root.

Falsifier tests from the design, using a throwaway root in a temporary directory: a valid token is accepted; a tampered agent_name is refused; an expired token is refused; a token for (worker-a, T-999, worker) presented as worker-b is refused; a set signed by a key that is not the enrolled root is refused. State whether nonces are single-use and test whichever you choose.
No wiring into blackboard.py or lock.py (that is T-454) and no change to any existing behavior. Do not edit CLAUDE.md. The suite passes via goal_mode. Hand off to verifier.
